# Writing prompts · ep04 · EPF ka byaaj FD se zyada? Safe options ki tulna.

The two writing steps of a new episode (MUSE.md → A new episode). Follow each prompt, put the answer into the files it names, upload them, and GitHub checks every number and word.

## Step 3 · Script prompt

```text
Write one Instagram Reel for PF Guru Ji Stories: a short story, told by a narrator in Hinglish, about one person from the cast who runs into a PF problem (a claim, a transfer, KYC, a new job) and gets through it the right way. The viewer sees themselves in the hero and learns what to do from the story, not from a lecture. Every person and place is drawn as a paper cut-out, so each line is a scene.
Topic: EPF ka byaaj FD, post office, PPF aur LIC se zyada kyun? Safe options ki seedhi tulna.
Viewer: A salaried person who keeps savings in FDs, the post office or an LIC policy, and is thinking of taking their PF out after changing jobs.
The cast (use only these people, by their names): shivam (Shivam: the hero of the stories: a young worker in his twenties, new to PF); priya (Priya: HR at Shivam's company: she knows the PF rules); ravi (Ravi: Shivam's friend, who learned the PF rules the hard way); papa (Papa: Shivam's father, retired after 30 years at a mill)
Language: Hinglish in Roman script. A narrator telling a friend's story: warm, quick, a little dramatic at the twist; not an ad, and not a government notice.

Use ONLY the numbers and rules in this data sheet. Each line is: id = value (kind).
- example_amount = ₹1,00,000 (assumption: say 'maan lo' or show EXAMPLE the first time) · The example sum kept for a year
- fd_rate = 6.4% (fact) · SBI's highest FD rate for the public (2 to under 3 years)
- ppf_rate = 7.1% (fact) · PPF interest rate, October–December 2026
- nsc_rate = 7.7% (fact) · NSC interest rate, October–December 2026
- scss_rate = 8.2% (fact) · Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme rate, October–December 2026
- ssy_rate = 8.2% (fact) · Sukanya Samriddhi rate, October–December 2026
- epf_rate = 8.25% (fact) · EPF interest rate for 2025-26
- fd_interest = ₹6,400 (derived: example_amount * fd_rate) · A year's interest on the example sum in the FD (simple)
- epf_interest = ₹8,250 (derived: example_amount * epf_rate) · A year's interest on the example sum in EPF (simple)
- extra_vs_fd = ₹1,850 (derived: epf_interest - fd_interest) · How much more EPF gives than the FD on the example sum in a year
- tax_free_limit = ₹2,50,000 (fact) · Yearly own contribution on which EPF interest stays tax-free (with an employer)
- lic_no_fixed_rate: An LIC endowment policy pays the sum assured plus bonuses that LIC declares each year from its experience; it has no fixed interest rate. (rule, from LIC's New Endowment Plan (Plan 714, UIN 512N277V03), sales brochure, from 22 September 2025)
- epf_interest_credit: EPF interest is fixed every year by the Central Government with the CBT, worked out on the monthly running balance and credited at the end of the year. (rule, from EPF Scheme, 2026, paragraph 42 (Gazette of India, G.S.R. 525(E), 29 June 2026))
- epf_tax_free: EPF interest is tax-free, except on a member's own contribution above ₹2,50,000 a year (₹5,00,000 with no employer contribution); bank FD interest is taxed as income from other sources. (rule, from Income-tax Act, 2025, Schedule II, entry 4 (EPF interest) and section 92 (income from other sources))
- transfer_on_job_change: On changing jobs, a member can move the old PF account to the new one (Form 13), so the money keeps earning EPF interest. (rule, from EPFO, 'Which claim form' (Form 13: moving an old PF account to the new one); brand/epfo-forms.json)
- passbook: The member's passbook on the member portal shows the contributions, the interest and the balance. (rule, from PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment, 18 September 2025: Passbook Lite on the member portal)
- scss_ssy_who: The post office's 8.2% schemes are the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (people aged 60 or more) and Sukanya Samriddhi (an account for a girl child). (rule, from India Post, savings schemes (Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme; Sukanya Samriddhi Account))
If you need a number, a limit, a waiting time or a rule that is not in the sheet, write [NEED DATA: what to find] instead. Never invent a statistic, a limit, a time or a rule.

The forms a reel may name, and what each one is for:
- Form 19: PF final settlement, by the member
- Form 10C: Pension (EPS) withdrawal benefit or scheme certificate
- Form 10D: Monthly pension
- Form 31: PF advance (partial withdrawal)
- Form 13: Moving an old PF account to the new one
- Form 20: PF settlement for the nominee or heir of a member who has died
- Form 5IF: EDLI insurance claim when a member dies in service

Rules:
1. 150–175 words in total (about 60–70 seconds at a brisk pace). Sentences of 3–9 words.
2. One line per shot, 14–18 shots, in this chapter order (the story's beats): hook, problem, why, steps, check, help, share, signoff.
   - hook (max 7 s): the hero's moment and the twist, in a line or two ("Shivam ne nayi naukri join ki. Pehle hi din, ek chhoti si galti.").
   - problem (max 10 s): what it costs the hero: money stuck, a claim back, months lost.
   - why (max 20 s): why it happened, only as EPFO's own rules say: someone who knows (Priya from HR, or Ravi) says it, or the narrator counts "Ek: … Do: …".
   - steps (max 25 s): what the hero does, in order, naming the real screens, menus and forms ("Member portal, Manage, phir KYC").
   - check (max 12 s): the one thing the hero checks, and what skipping it would have cost.
   - help (max 10 s): where the hero goes if it's still stuck: an official channel from the data sheet.
   - share: one line that ends "… abhi bhejo.", aimed at one kind of friend.
   - signoff: exactly "PF samjho, claim pao. EPFO ki har jankari chahiye? Follow karo PF Guru Ji."
3. The first time an assumption from the sheet is used, that line must say "maan lo".
4. EPFO rules:
   - Say only what EPFO's own pages, circulars and forms say, through the data sheet. Name a form only from the list above, and only for what it's for.
   - Never ask viewers for their UAN, password, OTP, Aadhaar, PAN or bank details: not in the reel, the caption or the pinned comment. The pinned comment may ask what went wrong, never for personal details.
   - Never promise an outcome or a date. A time limit is EPFO's rule from the data sheet, not a guarantee.
   - Send people only to official channels named in the data sheet: the member portal, the UMANG app, their EPFO office, the grievance portal. Never to an agent, a paid service, or a phone number that isn't in the sheet.
   - A phone number goes on a card, never in the voice line.
5. In "vo" (shown on screen as the captions), write Roman-script Hinglish, with numbers as digits, the ₹ sign and Indian commas (₹50,000, 1,00,000). Write forms as "Form 19", "Form 10C".
   In "tts" (read by the voice), write the same words in Devanagari, the script a Hindi voice reads correctly: every number said in English, the way people say numbers in Hinglish, and spelled in Devanagari (एट पॉइंट टू फ़ाइव परसेंट for 8.25%, वन लाख रुपीज़ for ₹1,00,000, एट थाउज़ेंड टू हंड्रेड फ़िफ़्टी for ₹8,250, ट्वेल्व महीने for 12 mahine; keep लाख and करोड़), and every English word spelled the way people in India say it (पीएफ, ईपीएफओ, क्लेम, फ़ॉर्म, केवाईसी, यूएएन, पोर्टल, फ़ॉलो, पीएफ गुरु जी). Say form names in English: Form 19 is फ़ॉर्म नाइनटीन, Form 10C is फ़ॉर्म टेन सी, Form 31 is फ़ॉर्म थर्टी वन. No digits, and no words that aren't in "vo". Use । for full stops, and let the punctuation carry the feeling: … for a held breath before a reveal, ! for a punch, ? for a real question.
6. "highlights" lists 1–3 words or numbers from the line to highlight in yellow, copied exactly from the line.
7. "uses" lists the data ids whose numbers appear in the line.
8. "delivery" says how the voice says the line: one mood (curious, surprised, excited, serious, concerned, warm, proud or playful), then " · " and one short cue: what to stress, where the energy goes up. Keep the pace brisk: the feeling comes from the voice, not from slowing down, so never write "slow down"; one held beat (…) at the big reveal at most. Change the mood from line to line, the way a friend telling a story would: a curious hook, a concerned problem, a proud answer, a warm share line. Never the same mood for every line.
9. Every line is new. TOPICS.md in the repo lists every reel we've made: never reuse a line, the hook or the cover from one of them, even with other numbers. Only the series formats repeat: "Ek: … Do: … Teen: …", the shape of the share line and the sign-off.
10. The caption ends with "EPFO ki har jankari chahiye? Follow karo @pfguruji.", then "PF Guru Ji EPFO ka official channel nahi hai. Niyam: epfo.gov.in", then the hashtags.
11. The story:
   - The hero is Shivam unless the topic needs someone else from the cast. Name each person the first time. A person speaks only in short quoted lines of 2 to 6 words, inside the narration ('HR ne poocha: "Purana UAN hai?"'): each one appears in a speech bubble.
   - One concrete place per beat: his home, the mill, HR's desk, the PF office, his phone. Things happen on the line's words: he walks in, his face falls, he checks his phone.
   - The hero learns and does the right thing; the story never laughs at the viewer.
   - A number in the story (his salary, how many months) is a data item like any other (input or assumption), and an assumption is said with "maan lo" the first time.
   - "scene" says, in one sentence for the reel writer, what the viewer sees on that line: who, where, doing what, and the words of any bubble (copied from the line).
12. Write two more hooks in "hook_options": other first lines for this reel, each from a different angle (a sharp question, the most surprising number in the sheet, the mistake the viewer is about to make), under the same rules as the hook. A person reads the script before anything is made, and picks one of the three or keeps yours.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"script": [{"shot": "S01", "chapter": "hook", "vo": "...", "tts": "...", "delivery": "curious · ...", "scene": "Shivam walks into the mill on his first day, smiling", "highlights": ["..."], "uses": ["..."]}],
 "hook_options": ["...", "..."],
 "post": {"caption": "...", "hashtags": ["#..."], "pinned_comment": "...", "cover": {"lines": ["...", "..."], "stamp": "..."}, "trial_hook": "..."}}
After the JSON, list every number you used and the data id it came from, and every form you named.
```

## Step 4 · Shots and reel.json prompt

Put `shots` and `breaks` into `episode.json`, and `reel` into `reel.json` (adding `"schema": "dc-reel/1"`, `"episode": "ep04-epf-interest-vs-fd"` and `"brand_label": "PF GURU JI"` at the top).

```text
REEL WRITER · PF Guru Ji Stories

Turn the approved story script below into the reel's shot list and its build file. Every shot is a paper cut-out scene: the cast as jointed paper puppets, the places and things as paper props, speech bubbles for what they say, and the series' cards and stamps for the numbers, all on the crumpled paper (see brand/assets/style-frames/cutout-demo.mp4 and its reel.json). tools/build_reel.py draws everything from your answer; paper, header, captions and sound are added for you. Be exact: every word on screen must come from that shot's card_text, every number from the episode's data, and every form name from brand/epfo-forms.json.

ANSWER WITH JSON ONLY, in three parts:
{"shots": [...], "breaks": [...], "reel": {"photos": {...}, "shots": {...}}}

1. "shots": one per script line, with the same ids, in the same order:
{"id": "S01", "start": 0, "end": 4, "chapter": "hook", "on_screen": "a short description for people", "card_text": ["every word or number on screen when the shot ends, exactly as drawn"], "motion_text": [], "uses": ["the data ids of every number in the line or on screen"], "yellow_elements": 1}
- Times: the first shot starts at 0 and each shot starts where the last one ended. Make each shot about (words in its line ÷ 2.6) + 0.5 seconds, rounded to 0.5. Give the last shot 3 extra seconds for the end card. The total must be 60–95 seconds; aim for about 70. (The build re-times every shot to the real voice later.)
- card_text: every string drawn in the shot, exactly. Numbers come only from the shot's "uses" data, with the ₹ sign and Indian commas (₹50,000, 1,00,000). The first card that shows an example number (a data item of kind "assumption") must say MAAN LO or EXAMPLE. Write forms as FORM 19, FORM 10C.
- motion_text: strings that are drawn but leave before the shot ends, such as a 3 WAJAH headline that slides away. They go here, not in card_text (the check reads card_text at the end of the shot). Usually empty.
- yellow_elements: how many yellow cards or tags the shot has. Never more than 1.

2. "breaks": the two torn-paper sheets that sweep across between chapters:
[{"after": "<last shot of the why chapter>", "at": <that shot's end time>, "type": "tear-lemon", "asset": "A08"},
 {"after": "<last shot of the check chapter>", "at": <that shot's end time>, "type": "tear-paper", "asset": "A09"}]

3. "reel": the build file.
- "photos": usually {}: the cut-outs need no photos. Only if a scene truly needs one (rarely), list it {"<short_id>": {"id": "P1", "file": "episodes/ep04-epf-interest-vs-fd/media/photos/<short_id>.webp", "alt": "what it shows, in a few words", "prompt": "..."}}. Write each prompt like this: "Black-and-white documentary photograph, landscape 4:3. <who or what, doing what, where in India>. <the light>, high contrast, fine film grain, eye-level camera, the subject in the middle of the frame. No text, no readable labels, no logos, no watermark." Never ask for signs, screens with writing, documents or forms with readable text, ID cards, passbooks, the EPFO logo or any government emblem.
- "screens": only for a reel that shows the member portal: every screenshot it uses, as {"<short_id>": {"id": "SC1", "file": "episodes/ep04-epf-interest-vs-fd/media/screens/<short_id>.png", "shows": "which page and what is open on it, for the person taking it", "must_show": ["each menu or button name the voice says on that screen, written as the portal writes it"]}}. A person takes them on their own login, with every personal detail covered; once one is uploaded, add "crop" ([x0, y0, x1, y1], shares of the image) to show only the part the line is about.
- "shots": {"S01": [elements], "S02": [elements], ...}: what each shot shows and when, built only from the blocks below. Elements are drawn in order: the first is at the back.

LAYOUT
Positions are pixels on the 1080×1920 frame. "x" is the horizontal centre (540 is the middle) and "y" is the top. Stamps, notes and bubbles use their centre (x, y); puppets and props stand on the ground line ("y" is where their feet or bottom are, 1170 by default). Everything goes between y = 400 and y = 1240: the header is above and the captions are below.
Two zones: the scene (y 640 to 1240): the ground, places, things and people; and above it (y 400 to 640): one card, stamp, headline or bubble at a time, never covering a face. A puppet at its usual scale (0.8) is about 500 px tall, its head near y 680.
Timing: "at" is seconds after the shot starts (the first element 0.1; the reel's very first element 0). "on" is a word from the shot's voice line (vo), copied with its punctuation if it has any ("Reject.", "Ek:"): the element lands as that word is spoken. Use "on" for every element after the first.
Entrances ("in"): rise (cards, the default), drop (photos and row cards), slide_left or slide_right (arrow cards and tags), slam (stamps, the default), pop (headlines, the default), write (notes, the default), none.
Tilt ("rot", degrees): cards −1.5 to 1.5, stamps 3 to 8 either way, notes −4 to −2.

- ground: {"type": "ground"}
  The torn paper strip the scene stands on. First in every scene shot. "color": "pencil" (the default) or "card".
- puppet: {"type": "puppet", "who": "shivam", "x": 300, "scale": 0.8, "facing": "right", "pose": "stand", "mood": "smile", "moves": [{"do": "walk", "to": 620, "dur": 1.4}, {"do": "pose", "pose": "wave", "on": "<word>"}, {"do": "mood", "mood": "worried", "on": "<word>"}]}
  A person from the cast (brand/brand.json → cast: shivam (Shivam: the hero of the stories: a young worker in his twenties, new to PF); priya (Priya: HR at Shivam's company: she knows the PF rules); ravi (Ravi: Shivam's friend, who learned the PF rules the hard way); papa (Papa: Shivam's father, retired after 30 years at a mill)), always the same look. Poses: stand, wave, point, think, phone, hips, cheer, shrug, hold, sad. Moods: neutral, smile, happy, worried, surprised, sad, angry, thinking. Moves land "on" a word (or "at" seconds after it appears): walk (to x; it faces the way it walks, about 280 px a second unless "dur" says), pose, mood, turn, jump, nod, shake. To enter, start off the frame (x −150 or 1230) and walk in; "in": "pop" (the default) to appear in place.
- prop: {"type": "prop", "kind": "office", "x": 760, "scale": 1.0, "label": "PF OFFICE", "variant": "tick", "idle": "sway"}
  A thing cut from paper: factory (smoke rises by itself), office, bank, home, phone (variant tick, alert, otp, chat or portal), document (variant rejected: a red cross), coins, calendar, laptop, tick, cross, clock (variant "4:30"; idle "spin": time passing), suitcase, cloud, sun, desk, skyline (a row of buildings far behind). "label" is the name on a factory, office or bank sign; "tab" a black label on any prop; both are card_text. "idle": sway, bob, buzz (a phone that rings) or spin. A prop on a desk or in a hand stands at that height: "y" is its bottom.
- bubble: {"type": "bubble", "text": "PURANA UAN HAI?", "x": 700, "y": 560, "tail": "down-right", "on": "<word>"}
  What a character says (or, with "thought": true, thinks), 2 to 6 words in capitals, above the speaker's head with the tail toward them ("left", "right", "down-left", "down-right"). Its text is card_text.
- photo: {"type": "photo", "src": "<short_id>", "tab": "TAB TEXT", "y": 400, "w": 960, "h": 560, "rot": -1.2}
  Rarely: a halftone photo with torn top and bottom edges.
- card: {"type": "card", "style": "white|yellow|black", "tab": "TAB TEXT", "prefix": "=", "big": "₹50,000", "label": "PF BALANCE\n(MAAN LO)", "foot": "small print", "size": 120, "y": 430, "w": 900, "h": 470}
  Big-number card: yellow, a tab, "big" at size 200–250, an optional "foot", h 400–470.
  Row cards, in a stack of 2 or 3: white (the result yellow), "prefix" (÷ × = ≈ +) and "big" at size 120 and a "label", no tab, at y 420, 595, 770.
  Black card: a tab (drawn in yellow) and "big" in white, w 600–760, overlapping the bottom edge of a photo.
  Its card_text strings are: the tab; the prefix and big joined by a space ("= ₹50,000"); the label on one line (line breaks become spaces); the foot.
- stamp: {"type": "stamp", "text": "REJECT!", "color": "red|ink", "x": 900, "y": 735, "rot": 8, "size": 72}
  A short verdict: REJECT!, PEHLE YEH, FREE HAI. Red, or "ink" (black) for the good side of a comparison. Never on top of small print.
- headline: {"type": "headline", "lines": ["CLAIM", "REJECT?"], "x": 80, "y": 520, "size": 260, "underline": {"line": 1, "at": 1.0, "dur": 0.5}}
  Huge words straight on the paper, for a question or a turn: 1 or 2 lines of 1 to 3 words. card_text has each line, or the lines joined by a space. "underline" is optional (a yellow marker line with a loop).
- note: {"type": "note", "text": "employer se poochho", "color": "red|ink", "x": 320, "y": 1110, "size": 74, "rot": -3}
  A handwritten aside of 2 to 5 lowercase words.
- tag: {"type": "tag", "text": "SHARE ↗", "x": 760, "y": 905, "rot": -4, "size": 96}
  A yellow slap-on label of 1 to 3 words, over a photo's lower edge.
- funnel: {"type": "funnel", "tab": "CLAIM KA SAFAR", "y": 420, "w": 920, "rows": [{"text": "CLAIM FILED", "width": 1.0, "on": "file"}, {"text": "KYC CHECK", "width": 0.76, "on": "KYC"}, {"text": "SETTLED", "width": 0.58, "style": "yellow", "on": "settle"}]}
  Graph-paper card whose bars grow one by one as each stage is spoken.
- line_chart: {"type": "line_chart", "tab": "<WHAT> · <UNIT> · EXAMPLE", "start": {"value": "<first value>", "sub": "<WHEN>"}, "end": {"value": "<last value>", "sub": "<WHEN>"}, "y": 420, "w": 920, "h": 560, "draw_at": 0.6, "draw_dur": 1.5}
  A red line drawing itself from the start value down to the end value. Values come from the data.
- arrow_card: {"type": "arrow_card", "arrow": "→", "title": "BANK KYC", "sub": "VERIFIED NAHI", "style": "white|yellow", "y": 420, "w": 900, "in": "slide_left"}
  For a list of reasons or steps: three cards at y 420, 600 and 780, each "on" its Ek: / Do: / Teen: word, arrows → ↘ ↗, one of them yellow. The arrow symbol is its own card_text string.
- timeline: {"type": "timeline", "tab": "NAUKRI CHHODNE KE BAAD", "segments": [{"from": 0, "to": 0.5, "style": "yellow", "label": "<FIRST STRETCH>", "on": "<word>"}], "ticks": [{"text": "<number from the data>", "pos": 0}], "foot": "<the rule, in a few words>"}
  A bar that fills in segments (yellow, white, red), with tick numbers under it and a key. Use it for waiting times; every tick number comes from the data.
- typewriter: {"type": "typewriter", "tab": "CLAIM SE PEHLE", "lines": ["Bank KYC verified.", "Aadhaar UAN se linked.", "Exit date marked."], "highlight": "verified", "highlight_on": "verified", "type_at": 0.5, "line_every": 1.15}
  A checklist of 2 to 4 lines, at most 26 characters each, typed out with a highlighter swipe.
- screen: {"type": "screen", "src": "<short_id in screens>", "tab": "MEMBER PORTAL", "y": 420, "w": 880, "h": 760, "marks": [{"box": [0.05, 0.20, 0.60, 0.27], "text": "Claim (Form-31, 19, 10C & 10D)", "on": "Claim"}]}
  A portal screenshot on a white card, for the steps of a portal how-to: one screen per step. Each mark is a red ring (or "style": "lemon", a yellow highlight) that lands on its word, round the menu or button the line names. "box" is in shares of the cropped screenshot and "text" is exactly what's inside it on screen: the check reads the screenshot and gives the right box if it's off. The screenshot's own words aren't card text; only the tab is, so give the tab no number (PORTAL · LOGIN, not STEP 4). Never show anything personal. A screenshot shot stays at least 4.6 seconds ("hold" changes it), so the viewer can find the button.
- endcard: the sign-off shot only, always these two elements:
  {"type": "note", "text": "PF samjho, claim pao.", "color": "ink", "x": 540, "y": 760, "size": 124, "rot": -2, "at": 0.1, "dur": 1.0, "out": {"on": "EPFO"}}
  {"type": "endcard", "tagline": "PF samjho, claim pao.", "small": ["<the main source, like NIYAM: EPFO.GOV.IN>", "<what's an example, if anything is>", "EPFO KA OFFICIAL CHANNEL NAHI"], "y": 430, "on": "EPFO", "lead": -0.2, "cta_on": "Follow"}
  The end card draws the logo, the tagline, the follow line ("EPFO ki har jankari chahiye?" over a "FOLLOW @PFGURUJI" button that pops in on "Follow") and the small print. Its card_text is "PF samjho, claim pao.", "EPFO ki har jankari chahiye?", "FOLLOW @PFGURUJI" and the small lines.

HOW EACH CHAPTER LOOKS
Every shot is a scene from the story: the ground, where it happens (a prop), who is there (puppets), and what they do and say on the line's words, with a card or stamp above when a number or a verdict lands. Follow each line's "scene" from the script. The same person keeps the same place on the ground from one shot to the next while the scene continues; a new place starts with the hero walking in.
- hook: the hero in his world from the very first frame (ground, place and puppet with "at": 0 and "in": "none"), and the twist landing on its word: a bubble, or a red stamp above.
- problem: what happens to the hero: his mood turns worried or sad on the word, a document with variant rejected or a phone with variant alert, and a big yellow card (h 220 to 260, at y 400) with what it costs, an amount from the data.
- why: someone who knows explains: Priya (HR) or Ravi (a friend) in a bubble, or the reasons as arrow cards at the top ("Ek: … Do: …", y 400, 500, 600 with "w" 760) while the hero thinks below.
- steps: the hero does each step, one beat each: a phone (variant portal or otp) or a laptop for the member portal, a document for a form, the office for the PF office; a typewriter checklist card can sum the steps up. A portal screenshot only if the reel shows the portal, at the top with the hero small below (scale 0.6).
- check: a card with the one thing to check and a red stamp with what skipping it costs; the hero nods.
- help: the office or a phone with a card naming the official channel (from the data) and an ink stamp FREE HAI or OFFICIAL.
- share: the hero gives a phone to a friend (pose hold, a phone prop between them), a yellow "SHARE ↗" tag on "abhi" or "bhejo", and a red note naming who to send it to.
- signoff: the endcard pair above.
Each element lands on its own beat of the line: 2 to 6 elements per shot. At most one yellow element per shot. Red only for stamps, notes and the things that are red by nature (the factory door, the calendar, a cross).

CHECK BEFORE YOU ANSWER
- Every string you draw is in that shot's card_text or motion_text, character for character, and every card_text string is still on screen when the shot ends.

DATA SHEET:
- example_amount = ₹1,00,000 (assumption: say 'maan lo' or show EXAMPLE the first time) · The example sum kept for a year
- fd_rate = 6.4% (fact) · SBI's highest FD rate for the public (2 to under 3 years)
- ppf_rate = 7.1% (fact) · PPF interest rate, October–December 2026
- nsc_rate = 7.7% (fact) · NSC interest rate, October–December 2026
- scss_rate = 8.2% (fact) · Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme rate, October–December 2026
- ssy_rate = 8.2% (fact) · Sukanya Samriddhi rate, October–December 2026
- epf_rate = 8.25% (fact) · EPF interest rate for 2025-26
- fd_interest = ₹6,400 (derived: example_amount * fd_rate) · A year's interest on the example sum in the FD (simple)
- epf_interest = ₹8,250 (derived: example_amount * epf_rate) · A year's interest on the example sum in EPF (simple)
- extra_vs_fd = ₹1,850 (derived: epf_interest - fd_interest) · How much more EPF gives than the FD on the example sum in a year
- tax_free_limit = ₹2,50,000 (fact) · Yearly own contribution on which EPF interest stays tax-free (with an employer)
- lic_no_fixed_rate: An LIC endowment policy pays the sum assured plus bonuses that LIC declares each year from its experience; it has no fixed interest rate. (rule, from LIC's New Endowment Plan (Plan 714, UIN 512N277V03), sales brochure, from 22 September 2025)
- epf_interest_credit: EPF interest is fixed every year by the Central Government with the CBT, worked out on the monthly running balance and credited at the end of the year. (rule, from EPF Scheme, 2026, paragraph 42 (Gazette of India, G.S.R. 525(E), 29 June 2026))
- epf_tax_free: EPF interest is tax-free, except on a member's own contribution above ₹2,50,000 a year (₹5,00,000 with no employer contribution); bank FD interest is taxed as income from other sources. (rule, from Income-tax Act, 2025, Schedule II, entry 4 (EPF interest) and section 92 (income from other sources))
- transfer_on_job_change: On changing jobs, a member can move the old PF account to the new one (Form 13), so the money keeps earning EPF interest. (rule, from EPFO, 'Which claim form' (Form 13: moving an old PF account to the new one); brand/epfo-forms.json)
- passbook: The member's passbook on the member portal shows the contributions, the interest and the balance. (rule, from PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment, 18 September 2025: Passbook Lite on the member portal)
- scss_ssy_who: The post office's 8.2% schemes are the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (people aged 60 or more) and Sukanya Samriddhi (an account for a girl child). (rule, from India Post, savings schemes (Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme; Sukanya Samriddhi Account))
```
